job_title: Part time PPC Manager (Google & Bing Ads)
description: Role Overview: We are seeking an experienced PPC Manager to lead the development, execution, and optimization of paid search campaigns across both Google Ads and Bing Ads. The ideal candidate will have a hands-on understanding of both platforms and proven success managing large-scale, complex campaigns with significant budgets. You will be responsible for delivering results-driven campaigns that align with client goals while maintaining a deep understanding of industry best practices. Previous experience working at Google or a strong insider knowledge of Google Ads best practices is highly advantageous. As a PPC Manager, you’ll be the go-to expert for all things paid search and will have a direct impact on client performance. The role requires a strategic mindset, data-driven decision-making, and the ability to maintain clear and effective communication with both internal teams and clients. Key Responsibilities: 1. Paid Search Strategy & Execution: Campaign Development & Management: Develop, launch, and manage paid search campaigns on Google Ads and Bing Ads, ensuring they are aligned with client objectives and maximize ROI. This includes campaigns on Google Search, Display, YouTube, Shopping, and Bing Search. Keyword Research & Audience Targeting: Conduct extensive keyword research, competitor analysis, and audience segmentation to identify growth opportunities. Develop comprehensive strategies based on these insights to optimize targeting and bidding. Campaign Optimization: Continuously analyze and refine campaigns to improve performance metrics such as CPC, CTR, CPA, and ROAS. Implement A/B testing strategies for ad creatives, landing pages, and bidding strategies to maximize conversions. Ad Copy & Creative Strategy: Work closely with the creative team to ensure that ad copy, creatives, and landing pages are optimized for user engagement and aligned with campaign goals. 2. Client Communication & Consultation: Client Liaison: Serve as the main point of contact for clients, providing expert consultation on all Google Ads and Bing Ads strategies. Clearly communicate campaign progress, adjustments, and results to ensure client satisfaction and alignment with business objectives. Performance Reporting: Regularly prepare and present in-depth performance reports, including key performance metrics (CPC, CTR, CPA, ROAS) and actionable insights. Use these reports to showcase campaign successes and provide strategic recommendations for optimization. Strategic Guidance: Offer strategic recommendations to clients, advising on how to improve campaign performance, expand reach, or address performance challenges. Proactively identify opportunities for growth. Client Relationship Management: Build and nurture strong relationships with clients, becoming a trusted advisor on paid search and digital marketing. Ensure high levels of client satisfaction, resolve campaign-related issues, and manage client expectations effectively. 3. Budget Management & Performance Tracking: Budget Oversight: Manage and optimize client budgets across both Google Ads and Bing Ads to ensure campaigns are efficient and within budget. Track and report on budget pacing and ensure that client goals are met while maximizing ROI. Performance Tracking & Analysis: Utilize Google Analytics, Microsoft Advertising Intelligence, Google Tag Manager, and other analytics platforms to monitor campaign performance in real time. Assess KPIs such as CPC, CTR, CPA, and ROAS to ensure campaigns are delivering results within the defined parameters. Optimization: Make data-driven decisions to optimize campaigns for better performance. Adjust bids, keywords, targeting, and ads based on performance trends and competitive insights. 4. Collaboration & Cross-Functional Alignment: Team Collaboration: Work closely with the broader digital marketing team (SEO, Social Media, Creative, Web Development) to ensure that PPC campaigns are integrated into wider marketing and sales strategies. Align campaigns with broader business objectives, ensuring a cohesive approach across all digital channels. Stakeholder Coordination: Collaborate with internal stakeholders to ensure paid search efforts align with company goals and support sales or product launch strategies. Knowledge Sharing: Actively contribute to knowledge-sharing within the marketing team by educating peers about PPC best practices, emerging trends, and new tools or features in Google Ads and Bing Ads. 5. Industry Trend Awareness & Innovation: Stay Current with PPC Trends: Stay up-to-date with the latest Google Ads and Bing Ads updates, features, and best practices. Attend webinars, conferences, and industry events to keep ahead of emerging trends and leverage new opportunities for clients. Test New Strategies: Continuously evaluate and experiment with new tools, bidding strategies, and ad formats to ensure campaigns are always optimized and competitive. Propose new strategies to clients based on these findings. 6. Reporting & Data-Driven Insights: Regular Reporting: Create and maintain regular performance reports, dashboards, and presentations to track campaign progress, analyze performance trends, and showcase ROI. Present these findings in a clear, concise manner to clients and internal teams. Actionable Insights: Translate complex data into actionable insights that drive campaign improvements. Provide clear, data-backed recommendations to both internal and client stakeholders to guide future PPC strategies and decisions. Attribution & Conversion Tracking: Implement and manage proper tracking systems to measure campaign effectiveness and provide accurate reporting on conversions, revenue, and other key metrics. Qualifications: Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Marketing, Business, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience). Certifications in Google Ads and Bing Ads are a plus. Experience: Proven PPC Experience: Minimum of 3–5 years of hands-on experience managing PPC campaigns across Google Ads and Bing Ads. This includes experience in Google Search, Display, YouTube, Shopping, and Bing Search campaigns. Agency or Client Experience: Experience working in a client-facing role, ideally in a digital marketing agency, managing multiple PPC accounts with large-scale budgets. Experience at Google (Bonus): Previous experience working at Google or within a Google Partner agency is highly desirable, particularly if you have in-depth knowledge of Google Ads best practices, new features, and insights from working directly with the platform. Technical Skills: Google Ads & Bing Ads Expertise: Advanced proficiency in managing campaigns across Google Ads and Bing Ads, including search, display, shopping, remarketing, and video campaigns. Analytics Tools Proficiency: Strong working knowledge of Google Analytics, Microsoft Advertising Intelligence, Google Tag Manager, and other relevant analytics and tracking tools to measure, report, and optimize PPC campaign performance. Data Interpretation: Ability to analyze large datasets, interpret complex data, and turn insights into actionable strategies to optimize campaign performance. Soft Skills: Excellent Communication & Presentation Skills: Ability to explain complex PPC strategies and performance data in a clear, concise, and accessible manner for clients, internal teams, and stakeholders. Client Management Experience: Proven experience in building and nurturing strong client relationships. Ability to manage client expectations and resolve issues in a timely and professional manner. Problem-Solving & Proactive Mindset: Strong problem-solving skills, with a proactive approach to identifying and addressing campaign issues. Ability to think critically and take strategic action based on data. Attention to Detail: High attention to detail, ensuring that campaign elements are precise and accurately reflect client objectives, even when working with large volumes of data. How to Apply: If you’re an experienced PPC Manager looking for a new challenge, we want to hear from you! Please submit your resume, along with a cover letter outlining your relevant experience. Include any specific campaigns or achievements that highlight your expertise with Google Ads and Bing Ads.

This role is closer to a true marketing agency project manager (within a multi-service environment) than a basic coordinator. We need someone who can operate inside a complex ecosystem with frequent context switching, ambiguity, and multiple workstreams moving at once. The goal of this hire is not simply “keeping tasks organized.” The goal is meaningful operational lift: someone who can own timelines, unblock delivery, keep everyone aligned, and reduce the amount of context-loading and oversight required from senior tea ---------- mbers. title: Email Deliverability & Domain Reputation Specialist (GoHighLevel)
description: We send 50,000+ marketing/transactional email s per week and several thousand SMS messages through GoHighLevel (LC Email + LC Phone). Volume is increasing. We recently had a deliverability i ---------- that cost us thousands of dollars when webinar registrants stopped receiving event reminders. We need a true expert — not a generalist email marketer, not a funnel builder, not a "VA who has done some email ." A specialist who can keep our sending infrastructure healthy, run domain warmups properly, monitor reputation daily, and catch problems *before* they cost us money. --- What You'll Own - Daily monitoring of domain reputation across Google Postmaster Tools, Microsoft SNDS, and blacklist services - SPF / DKIM / DMARC configuration and ongoing alignment management - Setting up and warming dedicated sending subdomains - A2P 10DLC SMS campaign registration and ongoing compliance - Weekly bounce, complaint, and engagement reports with specific recommendations - Diagnosing and fixing deliverability i ---------- quickly - Running warmup tools (Mailreach / Warmup Inbox / Instantly / Smartlead) for new domains --- Required Experience - Hands-on management of high-volume sending (20K+/week or more) on GoHighLevel, Mailgun, SendGrid, or similar - Proven track record running domain warmup ramps from cold to production volume - Working knowledge of DNS — you can read and write SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records without help - Experience using Google Postmaster Tools and Microsoft SNDS in your daily workflow - A2P 10DLC campaign registration experience (through Twilio or TCR) - At least one example of a deliverability problem you diagnosed and recovered from --- How to Apply (READ CAREFULLY — generic applications will be rejected) In your application, answer all five of these questions. Skip any of them and we won't review your application. 1. Explain the difference between SPF *pass* and SPF *alignment*, and why DMARC cares about alignment. 2. Walk me through a 30-day warmup ramp for a brand-new subdomain that needs to handle 50,000 email s per week. Tell me Day 1 volumes, Day 30 volumes, who you send to during warmup, and what you monitor daily. 3. What's your exact process for checking sender reputation across Gmail and Outlook? Name the tools and the metrics you track. 4. Have you registered an A2P 10DLC campaign before? Walk me through the brand and campaign registration process. If you haven't done one, say so honestly — but know that this is required for the role. 5. Tell me about a specific time a domain you managed got blocked, blacklisted, or sent to spam. What was the root cause, how did you diagnose it, and what specific steps did you take to recover? "I checked the settings" is not an answer. --- We pay fairly, we move quickly, and we promote people who deliver. We do not waste time on applicants who exaggerate experience — your work-sample test will expose that fast, so please apply only if you have the actual skill. Full-time | $1,200/month to start ($1,500/month after 30-day trial with proven results)

You track where each client is in their 30-day onboarding, send the reminders, prep the worksheets, and follow up when something is sitting too long. You also help me with marketing prep, billing, scheduling, and the daily admin that keeps the business running. This is a coordination role. The strategy is mine. The execution belongs to both of us, and your job is to keep it moving every single day. What you will do in a typical week A normal week sits in five buckets. Some weeks you will be heavier in one bucket than another, depending on where clients are in their phase. 1. Client delivery and SOP execution ? Flag anything sitting longer than it should, before it slips into next week. 2. Marketing prep and content support ? Keep the client roster, contact info, contract dates, and renewal milestones current in our CRM. ?  Update Calendar and send invites to prospective clients. 4. Scheduling and client communication ?  Schedule and confirm discovery calls, kickoff calls, weekly 1:1s, and create meeting schedule for client working sessions based on where they are at, action item focused. ?  Respond to basic client admin questions in our shared chat (calendar links, file requests, login resets, meeting prep notes). ?  Send weekly recap notes to clients after each session, pulled from my call summaries. 5. Reporting and weekly review ?  Pull a Monday morning report on inquiries, bookings, payments, and client status so we start the week aligned. ?  Update our internal dashboard with week-over-week numbers. Who this role is for ?  You are organized to the point that an unchecked task feels physically uncomfortable. ? title: Video Editor + Social Media Operator
description: WHO WE ARE We’re not a typical health clinic. Averus Group operates two health and wellness brands — Cerebral Health and Magnolia Hyperbarics — delivering advanced neurological and physical treatments including PEMF, HBOT, and Neurofeedback. Our patients come to us when conventional medicine hasn’t worked. We get results because we hold ourselves to an exceptional standard across every function of the business — including marketing. We’re building an in-house team that owns outcomes, not just outputs. That means the people we hire aren’t task-completers — they’re operators who understand that the quality of their work directly affects whether a patient walks through our door and gets the help they need. THE ROLE Create content that moves people; and moves them to book. This is a combined role for someone who is equally strong in short-form video editing and organic social media management. You'll edit raw clinic footage from Cerebral Health and Magnolia Hyperbarics into platform-native content — and then own everything that happens after it's published. Community engagement, DM management, content calendar, lead routing, and monthly reporting — this is your function. You're not a content scheduler. You're the person who understands that a comment or a DM is a potential patient, and you act accordingly. The content you create is often the first thing a patient sees before d ---------- to book. When that content is compelling, accurate, and on-brand— people take action. That’s the standard we hold this role to. WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING Day-to-day, here's what this looks like. • Video Editing • Edit short-form video from raw clinic footage for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and Facebook . • Produce TikTok love letter format content — text-on-screen, B-roll driven — reducing on-camera dependency on clinicians. • Deliver completed edits by the morning after raw footage arrives — same-day turnaround is the standard. • Cut ad-specific edits separately from organic content — different objectives, different formats. • Produce myth/fact series, clinic walkthroughs, and patient education content from provided briefs. • Organic Social Management • Manage the content calendar across TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook for both Cerebral Health and Magnolia Hyperbarics. • Publish a minimum of 5 posts and 3–5 Stories per week on Instagram; minimum 3 posts per week on TikTok. • Respond to all comments and DMs within 2 hours during business hours. • Identify warm leads in DMs and route them to the right booking flow or front desk contact. • Maintain ManyChat automation flows in coordination with the CRM Specialist. • Content Coordination & Reporting • Coordinate with the clinic team to schedule raw footage recording sessions. • Track the incoming content pipeline — what's been filmed, edited, scheduled, and published. • Ensure all content aligns with brand voice before it goes ---------- compassionate, confident, expert. • Deliver a monthly social post-mortem with performance data and actionable recommendations. • Update the weekly scorecard with social metrics: reach, engagement rate, DM leads, follower quality. YOU'D BE A GREAT FIT IF... Two functions. One person. Both at a high level. • You live on TikTok and Instagram. Not as a casual scroller — as someone who studies hooks, watches what performs, and understands why. If you can't tell us what you watched this week, this isn't the role for you. • You can turn raw footage into a compelling Reel by tomorrow. Same-day turnaround isn't a stretch goal — it's a baseline. You're fast, organised, and your output is polished under pressure. • You write captions that sound like a person, not a brand deck. Warm, direct, and specific. Not "We're proud to offer world-class treatment!" — actual human language that connects. • You treat a DM like a sales conversation. You know the difference between a curious follower and someone who's ready to book. You route them correctly and you don't let warm leads go cold. • You understand what content can't say in healthcare. You know Meta's ad policies. You know what language flags a post. You don't need to learn this on the job. • You're strong in both editing and social — not just one. This is a combined role by design. If you're a great editor who doesn't manage communities — or a great community manager who can't edit — we'll hire those functions separately. WHAT YOU'LL GET We take care of the people who take care of our patients. • Paid Time Off — Recharge so you can perform at your best. We respect the time you take away from work. • Sick Days — When life happens, it happens. Take the time you need to recover without the pressure. • Fully Remote — Work remote with a team spread across time zones — autonomy and flexibility built in. • Real Growth — This is a growing organization. As both brands scale, so do the opportunities for the people building them. • A Team That Cares — We hire people who are bought into the mission. You'll work alongside others who understand why the work matters, not just what the work is. • A Greater Mission — Every qualified booking you drive is a patient who gets access to treatment that could change their life. That's not marketing copy — that's the reality of what we do. Ready to apply? Send us 3 short-form video samples (under 60 seconds each) and a content calendar or posting schedule you've managed. Show us your editing and your strategy — both matter equally here.
